title: Simple logic diagrams
starter: A cash machine checks that a card is present AND the PIN is correct before it pays out. Write down two more everyday decisions that need both conditions to be true.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: The AND gate
facts: The output is 1 (true) only if both inputs are 1.
In a Boolean expression: A AND B, or A ∧ B.
Think: 'A and B must both be true'.
stations.challenge: Give an everyday example of an AND decision.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: The output is 1 (true) only if both inputs are 1.
Also credit: In a Boolean expression: A AND B, or A ∧ B.

questions.q: When is the output of an AND gate 1?
Complete the truth table for A AND B. Click each ? to change it to 0 or 1.
questions.a: Truth table for Q = A AND B over 2 inputs (4 rows); output is 1 wherever the expression is true

stations.name: The OR gate
facts: The output is 1 if either input is 1, or both are.
In a Boolean expression: A OR B, or A ∨ B.
Think: 'at least one of them is true'.
stations.challenge: Give an everyday example of an OR decision.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: The output is 1 if either input is 1, or both are.
Also credit: In a Boolean expression: A OR B, or A ∨ B.

questions.q: When is the output of an OR gate 0?
Complete the truth table for A OR B.
questions.a: Truth table for Q = A OR B over 2 inputs (4 rows); output is 1 wherever the expression is true

stations.name: The NOT gate
facts: NOT has one input, and it reverses it: 1 becomes 0 and 0 becomes 1.
In a Boolean expression: NOT A, or ¬A.
The small circle on the symbol means 'invert'.
stations.challenge: Why does the NOT gate only have one input?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: NOT has one input, and it reverses it: 1 becomes 0 and 0 becomes 1.
Also credit: In a Boolean expression: NOT A, or ¬A.

questions.q: What does a NOT gate do?
questions.a: Reverses its input: 1 becomes 0, and 0 becomes 1

questions.q: Complete the truth table for NOT A.
questions.a: Truth table for Q = NOT A over 1 inputs (2 rows); output is 1 wherever the expression is true

stations.name: Symbols and pseudocode
facts: AND can be written ∧, OR can be written ∨, and NOT can be written ¬.
Programs use the same logic in if statements.
In the cash machine program, the card is present and the PIN matches, so the AND is true.
stations.challenge: What does the cash machine program output, and why?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: AND can be written ∧, OR can be written ∨, and NOT can be written ¬.
Also credit: Programs use the same logic in if statements.

questions.q: Match each symbol to its operator.
What does the cash machine program output?

stations.name: Two-level circuits
facts: Gates can feed into other gates.
In (A OR B) AND C, the brackets are worked out first: the OR gate feeds the AND gate.
Work from the inputs on the left to the output on the right.
stations.challenge: Build the circuits on the board: drag gates from the top and wire outputs to inputs.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Gates can feed into other gates.
Also credit: In (A OR B) AND C, the brackets are worked out first: the OR gate feeds the AND gate.

questions.q: Build the circuit for Q = A AND C.
questions.a: Any circuit equivalent to A AND C (the site accepts any layout that gives the same truth table)

questions.q: Build the circuit for Q = (A OR B) AND C.
questions.a: Any circuit equivalent to (A OR B) AND C (the site accepts any layout that gives the same truth table)

stations.name: NOT and brackets
facts: NOT is worked out before AND and OR, unless there are brackets.
NOT A OR B means (NOT A) OR B.
NOT (A AND B) means work out A AND B first, then reverse it.
stations.challenge: What's the difference between NOT A AND B and NOT (A AND B)?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: NOT is worked out before AND and OR, unless there are brackets.
Also credit: NOT A OR B means (NOT A) OR B.

questions.q: In NOT A OR B, which part is worked out first?
Build the circuit for Q = NOT A OR B.
questions.a: Any circuit equivalent to NOT A OR B (the site accepts any layout that gives the same truth table)

questions.q: Build the circuit for Q = NOT (A AND B).
questions.a: Any circuit equivalent to NOT (A AND B) (the site accepts any layout that gives the same truth table)

final.name: Final challenge: build and read

questions.q: Build the circuit for Q = (A AND B) OR (C AND D).
questions.a: Any circuit equivalent to (A AND B) OR (C AND D) (the site accepts any layout that gives the same truth table)

questions.q: Write the Boolean expression for this logic diagram.
questions.a: Q = NOT (A OR B) (or any equivalent expression)

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

exam.q: Draw the logic diagram for Q = NOT (P AND R).
points: Programs use the same logic in if statements.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 2.

exam.q: Give the output of an OR gate when its inputs are 0 and 1.
points: The output is 1 (true) only if both inputs are 1.
Work from the inputs on the left to the output on the right.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark for a correct answer.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
